evidence.experimental_conditions: Occupational exposure; concentrations kept below 1.5 mg/m³ (Bergman 1952); also observed at threshold limit of 1.5 mg/m³ (general experience).
evidence.support_text: Tetryl (tetryl) caused frequent skin sensitization in an ordnance plant with more than 1000 exposed workers at concentrations kept below 1.5 mg/m³, as reported by Bergman (1952). Additionally, the most frequent effect of tetryl inhalation is sensitization, and the 1.5 mg/m³ threshold is low enough to prevent injury but not sensitizations (paragraph 451).
